result.reason: All four items deal with the principle of ho'il biyado l'garsha extended to a husband's claim that he divorced his wife — exactly the content described in the 'Divorce Claim' prose.

The passage directly presents Rav Yitzchak bar Yosef's report of Rabbi Yochanan's ruling and Rav Sheshet's dismissive reaction, which is precisely what the prose under heading 0 ('Yitzchak's Rejection') describes.

The passage presents the Gemara's challenge to Rabbi Yochanan's ruling (that a husband is not believed) by citing a contradictory tradition in his name (that a husband IS believed), which is precisely the tension that the 'Lemafrea Lehaba' section resolves with the l'mafre'a/l'haba distinction.

Items 1-6 constitute the continuous discussion of 'mi palginan dibura' — the retroactive/prospective distinction, the Rav Mari/Rav Zevid dispute, Rava's adultery challenge, and the bitrei gufai resolution — which is precisely what candidate 1 ('Split Application') describes in its prose, while candidate 2 ('Adultery Parallel') covers only the final resolution that wraps up this passage.
The passage describes the dying man's statement that his wife is fit to marry a High Priest, which is exactly what the 'Wife Status' prose section discusses.

Both items together form the exact Rava-Abaye-Rava exchange about conflicting Rabbi Yochanan traditions and whether a resolution can be relied upon for practical ruling, which is precisely what candidate 1 ('Abbaye Challenge') describes in detail.

The passage contains both Rav Yosef's statement about the double grounds for permitting the wife (the presumption and the dying declaration) and Abaye's interjection about distant witnesses — the full exchange is the subject of the 'Dying Claim' section's prose, which describes exactly this scenario including Abaye's objection as part of the same narrative unit.

The passage directly presents Rav Yosef's response that witnesses are not present before us and Rabbi Ḥanina's ruling about distant witnesses, which is precisely what the 'No Rumors' section's prose describes and analyzes.
The passage contains exactly the Abaye/Rava exchange (hikalnu bishvuyah / chush lah) that candidate 0's prose directly discusses and contextualizes.

All three items form the continuous gemara discussion about Shimon's position — asking what the other brothers say, challenging with the inheritance clause, and resolving with 'we do not know' (eini yodeia) — which is precisely what candidate 2 'Eini Yodeia' describes in its prose.

The passage contains exactly the Rava-Abbaye dispute about 'mane li beyadcha eini yodeia' and the 'maneh le'acher beyadcha' distinction, which is precisely what the 'Bari Veshema' prose section describes in detail.

Both items directly discuss Rava's dilemma about natural appreciation (shevach me'aleihem) of property that returns to Reuven, the clarification about shevach hamagi'a liktefayim, and the teiku conclusion — all of which are precisely what the 'Shevach Value' prose describes.

The mishna text describes the case of a diatiki found bound to one's thigh being legally void, which directly matches the 'No Effect' section's prose about that exact scenario, including the phrase 'harei zeh einah klum.'
